title: Marketplace trust, billing scenarios, and tile variants (WIP)
body:
Purpose: working doc to capture a compact set of trust + billing scenarios we need to represent in tile copy, plus an operational checklist for accepting partners into the cloud marketplaces (AWS, Azure, GCP). This is intentionally pragmatic — prioritize clear cues for customers (SLA, data residency, support tier), and call out edge billing flows that frequently break integration tests.

Status notes (quick):
- Goal: concise tile copy variants + acceptance checklist for partner onboarding funnel.
- Audience: partner success, listing PM, engineering intake, legal (spot-check).
- Ownership: go-to-market (Maya) for copy + acceptance, eng-infra for technical validation.

High-level product positioning to surface on tile (one-liners to iterate):
- Option A (trust-first): "Redwood Inference — high-throughput LLM inference with SLA-backed latency and tenant isolation."
- Option B (cost-first): "Run LLM inference with predictable costs — reserved capacity, autoscaling, and batching optimizations."
- Option C (security-first): "Private deployments (VPC/on‑prem) with KMS & audit logs for regulated workloads."
- Option D (developer-first): "Same API locally, in your cloud, and on Redwood Dedicated — ship faster with production-grade inference."

Tile subtitle / kicker examples (short):
- "SLA-backed latency · Model catalog · Private deployments"
- "From hosted API to private VPC — predictable inference at scale"
- "Pay-as-you-go or reserved capacity — match your economics"

30–50 char tile descriptions (for constrained UI):
- "SLA-backed LLM inference for production apps"
- "Private VPC & on-prem inference with KMS"
- "Predictable throughput, lower per-token cost"

Billing and entitlement scenarios to call out (operationally important):
1) Trial -> Marketplace metered conversion
   - Trial provisioned via marketplace trial SKU (time-limited credits).
   - Edge: buyer signs up, uses trial credits, then purchases metered subscription — need to reconcile trial usage with vendor metering (some marketplaces do not surface trial usage in metered receipts).
   - Acceptance test: verify trial->metered invoice mapping for both aggregated and per-customer breakdowns.
2) Reserved capacity (Dedicated) purchased through reseller/channel
   - Reserved contract bought via marketplace might be a purchase order handled outside cloud metering (direct invoice). Ensure entitlement system maps marketplace purchaser to an org with committed capacity.
   - Edge: reseller transfer of entitlement to downstream customer (reseller model).
3) BYOK/KMS + Marketplace billing
   - Customer uses their KMS. Contract has explicit billing via marketplace, but encryption keys are customer-managed — ensure onboarding doc clarifies that KMS provisioning must happen before provisioning Private deployment.
4) Multi-tenant vs single-tenant SLAs
   - Marketplace tile must not promise SLA for hosted offer unless plan is backed by Dedicated reservation or explicit SLA add-on.

Operational acceptance checklist (pre-publish):
- Copy & assets
  - [ ] Title and 1-line + 3 subtitle variants reviewed by PM & legal
  - [ ] 120×120 logo + square/retina assets submitted (png/svg)
  - [ ] Short description (<= 200 chars) and long description (<= 2,000 chars) uploaded
  - [ ] 2–3 screenshots / diagrams showing console, API call, and telemetry
- Technical gating
  - [ ] KMS/BYOK compatibility doc attached (if private offer)
  - [ ] Network topology notes for private and VPC connectors (expected IP ranges)
  - [ ] Compatibility matrix: AWS/Azure/GCP region parity noted
  - [ ] Verified that dedicated SKU maps to internal capacity pool ID (for billing)
- Legal & compliance
  - [ ] Standard T&C accepted; exceptions tracked in vendor/contract doc
  - [ ] Data residency claim verified with infra (regions + logs retention)
  - [ ] SOC2 status + SOC2 expiration date added to metadata
- Billing & metering tests
  - [ ] Trial issuance and redemption tested end-to-end
  - [ ] Metering events from runtime are received by billing pipeline (sample CSV/JSON verified)
  - [ ] Reserved capacity entitlements correctly produce commitment invoices
- Support & escalation
  - [ ] Support tier captured on tile (email + SLA hours)
  - [ ] On-call escalation path documented (pager/email/Slack)
- Launch readiness
  - [ ] Internal playbook for lead routing to AE/SE/CS
  - [ ] Marketing one-pager + 2 demo scenarios for trial sign-up

Telemetry & runtime checks (DEV/ENG):
- Sampling: ensure the runtime emits a marketplace-customer id in request headers for attribution
- Probe: a dedicated smoke test that executes a short chat generation and validates tokens and latency against thresholds
- Billing sandbox: mirror metering events to staging billing pipeline for validation

Copy variants for marketplace tile (short, medium, long):
- Short (30–60 chars): "Production LLM inference: low latency, predictable cost, private options"
- Medium (100–140 chars): "Run and scale LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. SLA-backed throughput, model catalog, and developer SDKs for fast integration."
- Long (<= 2,000 chars draft): "Redwood Inference provides a unified runtime for running LLMs in production — whether you want the simplicity of a hosted API, the predictability of Dedicated reserved capacity, or the control of private VPC/on-prem deployments. Our platform optimizes latency and cost via intelligent batching, KV caching, and optimized kernels. Get observability per-route, canary rollouts, and enterprise-grade controls (KMS, audit logs, region pinning) to meet regulated workloads. Choose pay-as-you-go metered billing or reserved capacity with commitment discounts."

Sample marketplace FAQ snippets (for listing page):
Q: "What SLAs are included?"
A: "Hosted API tiers have best-effort SLAs; dedicated/reserved offers include clearly documented uptime and latency targets — see SLA add-on in the pricing section."

Q: "Can I use my KMS?"
A: "Yes — private offers and VPC deployments support BYOK/KMS. Contact engineering to schedule the KMS key trust exchange as part of onboarding."

Q: "How do I migrate from hosted to dedicated?"
A: "Same API surface. Open a ticket with CS to initiate capacity mapping; we support live traffic cutover with canary routing and fallback to hosted instances."

Decision log / open questions (short):
- D1: Do we surface latency SLA on tile for "Hosted Pro"? (open for legal/ops)
- D2: How explicit should we be about quantization / model quality tradeoffs in tile copy vs long description? (product)
- Q1: marketplace trial accounting across cloud providers — which providers surface trial usage in billing export? (eng + billing)
- Q2: reseller flow for reserved capacity — do we allow transfer of commitment credits or only seat-level transfers? (legal + finance)

Next steps / owners:
- Maya: iterate 3 final tile copy lines and send to legal (due 2024-09-25)
- Jordan: validate metering events for trial scenario in staging (ENG-1129) (due 2024-09-30)
- Ava: collect SOC2 cert and data residency proof for listing metadata (due 2024-10-04)

Notes to self / scratchpad:
- Consider adding a tiny "how we price" explainer image for the tile (reserved vs metered).
- Keep tile conservative on promises — avoid SLA guarantees for hosted unless we can link to an explicit plan.
- Save final copy variations in github repo /marketplace-assets under a new folder for A/B tests.

-- end working draft --
